title: Keep the analyzer working when source generation is suppressed

lines.text: > Note: When using Unity, dynamic code generation only works when targeting .NET Framework 4.x + mono runtime.
For all other Unity targets, AOT is required.
A `[MessagePackObject]` type can opt out of source generation with `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`.
No formatter is generated for that type. It is serialized at run time by the dynamic resolvers, which use reflection, so such a type is not AOT-safe.
The analyzer still validates these types, because they are serialized at run time and must still have a valid contract:
- Keys are unique and all of the same kind ([MsgPack005](doc/analyzers/MsgPack005.md)).
- Members have types that are themselves serializable ([MsgPack003](doc/analyzers/MsgPack003.md)).
- Types are accessible to the resolver ([MsgPack012](doc/analyzers/MsgPack012.md)).

The analyzer does not report the partial-class requirement ([MsgPack011](doc/analyzers/MsgPack011.md)) or the AOT-only checks ([MsgPack016](doc/analyzers/MsgPack016.md) and [MsgPack017](doc/analyzers/MsgPack017.md)) for these types, because they only apply when a formatter is generated.
You can customize the generated source through properties on the `GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute`.

requirement.title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement.intent: The analyzer must report its diagnostics for types that set SuppressSourceGeneration = true, as it did in version 3.1.0.

functional.text: The analyzer reports diagnostics for a [MessagePackObject] type with SuppressSourceGeneration = true.
The analyzer behaves for such types as it did in version 3.1.0, before the regression in 3.1.1.

nonFunctional.text: The analyzer must not crash on invalid input in a suppressed type; it reports the problem instead. (inferred)
Types that do not suppress source generation keep their current diagnostics. (inferred)

derivedFrom.note: Derived by the engine lane from the upstream issue text on 2026-11-14; not Tieto's requirements set.

expectedBehaviours: A [MessagePackObject] type with SuppressSourceGeneration = true that breaks an analyzer rule (for example a public member without a [Key] attribute) gets the matching MsgPack diagnostic in the IDE and in the build output.
Diagnostics for suppressed types show up whether or not the source generator writes a formatter for that type.
Setting SuppressSourceGeneration = true still stops formatter generation for that type. Only the analysis comes back, not code generation.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] type that has a member missing its [Key] attribute expects the corresponding MsgPack diagnostic at that member.
A generator snapshot test confirms that no formatter is generated for the suppressed type, while the analyzer test for the same type still reports its diagnostics.

expectedBehaviours: For suppressed types, the analyzer reports the same diagnostic IDs at the same locations as version 3.1.0 did.
Diagnostics that went silent for suppressed types in 3.1.1 are reported again, and no new diagnostic appears that 3.1.0 did not produce for these types.
Any code fixes that worked on these diagnostics in 3.1.0 are offered again for suppressed types.
expectedTests: A regression test covers the scenario from the issue: a suppressed type that produced diagnostics in 3.1.0 must produce the same diagnostics now.
A test runs the same invalid type definition with and without SuppressSourceGeneration = true and expects the same set of analyzer diagnostics in both cases.

expectedBehaviours: A suppressed type with invalid input, such as duplicate keys, bad key types or inaccessible members, gets a diagnostic. The analyzer does not crash.
The build never shows an AD0001 analyzer exception warning, and no exception escapes the analyzer for suppressed types with malformed input.
Analysis of the other types in the same compilation keeps running when one suppressed type is invalid.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a suppressed type that has duplicate [Key] values expects the duplicate-key diagnostic and no AD0001 or other exception diagnostic.
An analyzer test with a suppressed type mixing int and string keys, or with an unsupported member, expects a reported diagnostic and a compilation that finishes without an analyzer exception.

expectedBehaviours: Types that do not set SuppressSourceGeneration, or set it to false, report exactly the same diagnostics as before the change.
Generated formatters and resolvers for unsuppressed types are unchanged, and the existing generator snapshot outputs under Resources still match.
Diagnostics are not reported twice for any type.
expectedTests: The existing analyzer test suite for unsuppressed types passes without changes to the expected diagnostics.
The existing generator snapshot tests pass without updating the expected output files.
A test with an invalid unsuppressed type checks that each expected diagnostic is reported exactly once.

story.what: In TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo the change protects the int-key and string-key member dictionaries against duplicate keys. A member is now added only when its key is not already present, so Dictionary.Add can no longer throw. When a member's key kind (int or string) does not match the earlier members, the collector now reports DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys and skips that member with continue, so it no longer goes on into code that unwraps a null key. The change also inverts the condition in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol that reports a formatter's InaccessibleDescriptor diagnostic. It adds a README section on SuppressSourceGeneration, analyzer tests for suppressed types, and execution tests that check a suppressed type gets no generated formatter but still round-trips.
story.why: Issue 2234 reports that the analyzer stopped reporting diagnostics for [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] types after 3.1.0. With invalid key definitions, such as duplicate or mixed keys, the collector could throw during analysis. The change makes the collector report those problems and keep going, so the rest of the validation, which runs before the suppressSourceGeneration early return, still produces its diagnostics.

touches.note: Condition for reporting a formatter's InaccessibleDescriptor flipped from !ExcludeFromSourceGeneratedResolver to ExcludeFromSourceGeneratedResolver.
Skips members with a mismatched key kind after reporting the diagnostic, and guards intMembers/stringMembers Add calls with ContainsKey, for both properties and fields.
New analyzer tests for suppressed types: MsgPack004, 015, 003, duplicate and mixed keys (005), and no 011/016/017.
New execution tests: no generated formatter for a suppressed type, and a round trip through the standard options.

findings.title: Inaccessible-formatter diagnostic condition inverted without requirement
findings.detail: In AnalyzeSymbol, the check that reports a formatter's InaccessibleDescriptor (MsgPack010 or MsgPack013) changed from !formatter.ExcludeFromSourceGeneratedResolver to formatter.ExcludeFromSourceGeneratedResolver. Formatters that the generated resolver should pick up but cannot reach (non-internal type, no usable constructor or Instance field) no longer get a warning, so they are dropped from the resolver without notice. Formatters the user explicitly excluded now get warnings that no longer apply to them. The requirement does not ask for this change. It has nothing to do with SuppressSourceGeneration, it changes diagnostics for types that do not suppress generation (against N2), and no test or README text covers it.

findings.title: Mixed-key member skip also skips member type validation
findings.detail: The new continue after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys skips the rest of the loop body, including the recursive CollectCore(item.Type, item) call. A property or field with a mismatched key kind is therefore never checked further. For example, MsgPack003 is no longer reported when its type is not serializable, which hides a real problem until the mixed-key error is fixed. Only the dictionary insert needed skipping. The type collection could still run.

citations.quote: continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.

findings.title: Field with null key still crashes the analyzer
findings.detail: N1 requires that invalid input in a suppressed type is reported, not crashed on. If the first keyed field has [Key(null)] (string overload with a null value), BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull is reported and isIntKey becomes false. Execution then reaches the field else branch, which calls stringMembers.ContainsKey(stringKey!) with null and throws ArgumentNullException, giving AD0001. The property path guards this with 'else if (stringKey is not null)', but the field path has no such guard, and the change leaves it as it is.

findings.title: Field-side guards and code fixes for suppressed types untested
findings.detail: Every new analyzer test uses properties, so the field-side changes (continue on mixed key kinds, ContainsKey guards for duplicate int and string keys) are never exercised. Also, no test sets FixedCode to check that the MsgPack004 code fix is offered again for a suppressed type, as it was in 3.1.0, even though the tests already use the code-fix verifier.
